drafted_from: tool:find-events-against-a-running-baseline's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-events.mjs, tools/media-composition/test/stream-core.test.mjs (its real-clip test uses the same 26 second clip), and the script run on that clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find every stroke in my rally video, judged against how loud and busy the video already is." It runs tool:find-events-against-a-running-baseline and hands back each event's time and confidence.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name by its file identity and answers from that video alone, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your video's identity in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.

2. Say "Find the events in this video against its own baseline" with that identity. The default detector is adaptive; give detector "sound-and-motion" to rank the sharpest sound with movement instead. Add from and to (seconds) to search a stretch.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:find-events-against-a-running-baseline. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.events: each has kind, time (seconds in the video) and confidence 0 to 1. An empty events list means nothing stood out; it is not an error.
